translation.en:
38

Most gracious Prince and Lord, after all the vexation, which has quite undermined my health, I lie wretchedly ill and [uncertain: kunde] cannot write much. Only this for now: I have received the 3,000 Rthl from the banker Veit, and only yesterday delivered the order to pay to Amelang.

Now I must still raise another 3,000 Rthl, for the treasury received 5,125 Rthl; of the 2/m I had only 3,000 Rthl. I had to borrow through the help of His Excellency the Minister von Zastrow; one gave papers, we must [have] Courant it seems — these were now 5,176 Rthl of new debt, which I have now had to discharge, so I have taken your 3,000 Rthl for it. 2,176 Rthl I thought to obtain upon the papers which Hecker had deposited as security; in the meantime, however, the papers had so fallen that upon 4,000 Rthl of Märck Landschaft obligations no one would give even 500 Rthl.

The tavern too had some 2,003[?] rt to pay on account of the defraying of the military execution; that now amounted afresh to 4,209 Rthl Courant, which in these ghastly times were not to be raised — papers I could obtain, if I were willing to give Courant for them — that would then have come to 21,000 Rthl. God helped me meanwhile: the Baupiner or Later took wood and boards from Konotop instead of money — by this means the 4,176 Rthl will be discharged, and the Minister Zastrow already has his papers back — I suffer 3,480 Rthl of loss on the wood, for I had to let it go at half price — this Your Serene Highness must one day make good to me. This loss is small against 25,000 Rthl — As to the dahrliche let Your Serene Highness indeed take care — for you pay with 20,000 Rthl in cash now hindert laufend that is — could you raise 150,000 Rthl there, then you have papers to the value of 750,000 Rthl and with them pay all your debts.

I can write no more today, I am too feeble; more in future — I am ever Your Serene Highness's

As soon as I have been, and I can quickly raise the Weise money, then I shall go to Vienna, and if it can be managed I shall come to Öhringen; but if business does not allow it, I shall return hither and write. Only let Your Serene Highness take care that you obtain 150,000 Rthl, then Courland and all the stuff is paid. But it requires haste, the papers are rising wirdet. Berlin, the 14th of June

1808.

most faithful servant

v Triebenfeld

Something great must be afoot in the country: the Russian papers have risen unspeakably on the 8th of this month in Wrocław itself. There they hold the peace between Russia and England for certain. Now of our court I will say nothing. St: conducts himself badly, and by his money-in-paper manoeuvres he tears apart the last bond between the King and the nation. Also for the house St: only friendship —

summary_en: Triebenfeld, seriously ill, reports the receipt of 3,000 Rthl from the banker Veit and the handing over of the order of payment to Amelang. He says he has used it to pay off part of new debts of 5,176 Rthl. Instead of money, timber and boards from Konotop were accepted, with which 4,176 Rthl are to be paid off. He says the Prince should make good to him the loss of 3,480 Rthl. He advises raising 150,000 Rthl in order to acquire papers worth 750,000 Rthl and pay all the debts.
summary_de: Triebenfeld, schwer krank, meldet den Empfang von 3000 Rthl vom Bankier Veit und die Übergabe der Anweisung an Amelang. Neue Schulden von 5176 Rthl habe er damit teils getilgt. Statt Geld wurden Holz und Bretter aus Konotop angenommen, womit 4176 Rthl getilgt werden sollen. Den Verlust von 3480 Rthl soll der Fürst ihm ersetzen. Er rät, 150000 Rthl aufzubringen, um für 750000 Rthl Papiere zu erwerben und alle Schulden zu bezahlen.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld writes to the Prince from Berlin. He is ill and keeps it short. He has received 3000 rt from the banker Veit and handed the Anweisung to Amelang. He explains his debts: 5176 rt of new debt, borrowed with Zastrow's help. Hecker's caution papers have lost value, and a total of 4209 rt cannot be raised in cash. Wood and boards from Konotop were taken instead of money, which pays off 4176 rt, and Zastrow has his papers back. He loses 3480 rt on the wood and asks to be reimbursed. He advises the Prince to raise 150000 rt, which would buy 750000 rt in papers and pay all debts. He plans to go to Vienna and perhaps Öhringen. Nothing on Trąbczyn.

claims.statement: 3000 Rthl vom Bankier Veit erhalten, Anweisung an Amelang abgegeben
neue Schulden von 5176 Rthl, mit Hilfe Zastrows geliehen, mit den 3000 Rthl des Fürsten teils getilgt
claims.why: Laut Z. 8 hat er mit Zastrows Hilfe nur 3000 Rthl geliehen. Die 5176 Rthl sind die neuen Schulden insgesamt (Z. 9). Die Zuordnung zu Zastrow gehört also zu einer anderen Summe. Belegt ist, dass er die 3000 Rthl des Fürsten zur Tilgung genommen hat.

claims.statement: Holz und Bretter aus Konotop statt Geld angenommen, 4176 Rthl werden getilgt
Verlust von 3480 Rthl am Holz soll der Fürst ersetzen
Rat, 150000 Rthl aufzubringen, dafür 750000 Rthl Papiere, damit alle Schulden bezahlen

claims.why: Z. 26-27: Die Reise ist an eine Bedingung geknüpft, nämlich dass er das Geld schnell aufbringen kann.

doubtful_words.note: garbled; a buyer or creditor who took wood instead of money
